text.headline: Timeline of Lesotho
text.text: Major events in the history of Lesotho.

events.headline: Earliest Inhabitants
events.text: The region that is now Lesotho was inhabited by the San people, known for their rock art and hunter-gatherer lifestyle.

events.headline: Formation of Basotho Nation
events.text: Moshoeshoe I, a chief of the Basotho, began to consolidate various clans into a single nation, establishing the foundation of modern Lesotho.

events.headline: Battle of Viervoet
events.text: The Basotho fought against the Nguni tribes in the Battle of Viervoet, marking a significant conflict in the consolidation of the Basotho nation.

events.headline: British Protectorate
events.text: Lesotho became a British protectorate after a series of conflicts with the Cape Colony, leading to the establishment of colonial rule.

events.headline: Formal Annexation
events.text: The British formally annexed Lesotho, incorporating it into the Cape Colony, which led to increased tensions with the Basotho people.

events.headline: Independence from Britain
events.text: Lesotho gained independence from British colonial rule, becoming a constitutional monarchy under King Moshoeshoe II.

events.headline: Political Turmoil
events.text: The 1970 elections were annulled by Prime Minister Leabua Jonathan, leading to political unrest and the establishment of a one-party state.

events.headline: Military Coup
events.text: A military coup led by General Justin Lekhanya overthrew the government, marking the beginning of military rule in Lesotho.

events.headline: Return to Democracy
events.text: Lesotho held its first democratic elections after years of military rule, leading to the establishment of a parliamentary democracy.

events.headline: Political Violence
events.text: Political unrest and violence erupted following disputed elections, leading to military intervention by South Africa.

events.headline: Constitutional Reforms
events.text: Lesotho adopted a new constitution aimed at strengthening democratic institutions and promoting human rights.

events.headline: Economic Challenges
events.text: Lesotho faced significant economic challenges, including high unemployment and reliance on remittances from migrant workers in South Africa.

events.headline: Political Crisis
events.text: A political crisis emerged when Prime Minister Thomas Thabane suspended parliament, leading to widespread protests and calls for reform.

events.headline: Security Sector Reforms
events.text: Lesotho initiated security sector reforms to address issues of political instability and improve governance.

events.headline: Thabane Returns to Power
events.text: Thomas Thabane returned to power after a coalition government was formed, aiming to stabilize the political situation in Lesotho.

events.headline: COVID-19 Pandemic
events.text: Lesotho faced challenges due to the COVID-19 pandemic, impacting its economy and healthcare system significantly.

events.headline: General Elections
events.text: Lesotho held general elections, which resulted in a coalition government, reflecting the ongoing political dynamics in the country.

events.headline: Continued Political Reforms
events.text: Lesotho continues to pursue political reforms aimed at enhancing governance and stability in the wake of recent elections.
